turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in here today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I've had this cough ongoing for a couple of months now, uhm, and recently I've started to notice some blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so this cough has been going on for how many months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say maybe six months.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Six months, and have you had this cough before, then?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've had a cough before and kind of for a long time, 'cause I've smoked for a while.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see, Uhm, what kind of cough do you have, is it productive? Like, is it a wet cough or is it a dry cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's usually a dry cough, but recently I've been bringing up a little bit of blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is the blood mixed in with like sputum that you're bringing out or is it that you're just coughing up blood?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's mostly red, yeah, mostly blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see, and is your coughing constant or does it come and go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's kind of like, constant throughout the day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you noticed any kind of greenish or yellowish color of your sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not really, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How much blood would you say you're coughing up now in an average day?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say, maybe two or three teaspoons.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see. Has your coughing gotten worse or has it stayed about the same?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's been about the same.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, is there anything that makes your symptoms better or worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not really, it's just kind of been there most days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you have any other symptoms like shortness of breath or chest pain, runny nose, anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm No, no I haven't really had anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so with your coughing, you don't feel like you have any difficulty breathing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I mean, I haven't had any shortness of breath, I've just had uh, well yeah, actually sorry, I have had difficulties breathing as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when did that start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, well that's been an ongoing problem for the last several years now, I thought it was related to smoking, but it's gotten worse.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK, and do you have any chest pain with inspiration or expiration?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no chest pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any dizziness? Any fainting episodes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any recent travel outside of the country?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've been at home.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any headaches, fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no fevers or chills, and I haven't had any headaches either.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any losses in sense of taste or smell?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, yeah, I have been a bit more nauseous recently, but I haven't had any vomiting.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when did you start feeling nauseous?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It kinda comes and goes, I've had that problem for the last two months or so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you feel nauseous at anytime particularly in the day, like after eating, Or does it just come on randomly?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Randomly.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you been having any kind of diarrhea or Constipation, changes in your bowel movement?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any blood in your stools at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you been feeling fatigued at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, a little bit more tired recently, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how recently would you say?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I thought it was related to like, just being short of breath, Yeah, so maybe in the last couple of months as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when do you get short of breath? Is it when you do any activities? Is it when you're laying down? Is there anything related to it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: If I exert myself or if I'm  doing more activity, it it does get harder to to keep up with it, but yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you notice you have to like get up at night to take a breath? Or when you're laying down,do you have any trouble breathing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you noticed any kind of swelling in your extremities or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No swelling.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had any night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about your sleep and appetite, have they changed it all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, my appetite's been less. I've lost some weight over the last few months.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how much weight would you say you've lost?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Maybe ten to fifteen pounds.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how much do you weigh?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think now I weigh about one hundred and sixty pounds.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so yeah, ten to fifteen pounds in the last, how many months would you say?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Maybe two months.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Two months, OK. Have you recently had any infections, like viral symptoms, like runny nose, fever, or any cold like symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any exposure to anyone that you know of that might have tuberculosis?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've been been mostly at home. I Haven't really been seeing many people lately.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you have any past medical history or any diagnosis like COPD, asthma, high blood pressure, diabetes, anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I had a cataract surgery, but that's about it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are there any medications that you take on a daily basis?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Multi-vitamins.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Multi vitamins, OK, any allergies that you know of to medications or any environmental allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think sulfa, but that's it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what kind of reaction do you get?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I get a rash.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Rash, OK, any surgeries or hospitalizations in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I just had cataract removed from my right eye, and uh, that's about it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any Contacts of yours that have been sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK, and in terms of your family history, are there any cancers like lung cancer in your family or any heart conditions, anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think my great uncle had lung cancer, my mom had type 2 diabetes, but that's it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and currently right now, do you work?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I'm retiring soon. I work as a bus driver.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and in the past have you worked in any environment where you were exposed to any metals, toxins, any asbestos or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I worked as a bus driver for quite a number of years now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And where do you live right now? In an apartment? In a home? And who do you live with?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I live in a home with my wife and it's just us two.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you know if there's any like asbestos exposure in your home at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and currently do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've been cutting down, but I do smoke, yes. I smoke about a half a pack per day now. There was a time I was smoking two packs per day for a number of years and I started smoking when I was probably fifteen.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Mhm.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so it's been about forty, Yeah, forty-ish years at least.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you thought of quitting at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've been trying. I was thinking of maybe talking about a prescription for helping quit or something like that today. I was feeling like this is causing some of my symptoms like my cough, shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, well, it's really great that you're thinking about quitting. We can definitely help you with some resources, and some medications. Have you tried anything before that I should know of, to help you quit?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've tried nicotine patches and gum, but that's it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so yeah, there's uh, like other options as well that you can take. Have you heard of Champix?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I did hear of it actually. Yeah, so one of my friends tried it and it worked well for them so, Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah, so we can, if you're wondering about that, I can give you some information on that medication, like a whole package for you and then we can discuss if that could work for you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That sounds great.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sweet. And other than smoking, do you use any recreational drugs like marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well I'll have one or two beers on the weekend.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, so yeah, that's pretty much all the questions I had right now. It seems that your symptoms, You do have that cough and the shortness of breath and it's been chronic, but now you're coughing up some blood as well, so that is definitely something that's concerning and we want to make sure there is nothing going on so we will get a chest X-ray for you and see if we can find anything there. Are still producing the bloody sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that's been coming up a daily still.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so if you think you can produce that, we can even take a sample of that as well and see if there is any presence. The one thing that we are concerned about with some of your symptoms and a long history of smoking as well is lung cancer. So yeah, we will do a chest X-ray, get some cytology done as well and then once we have that in the future we may need to maybe do a biopsy but right now we'll do a few of the first things that I mentioned and then go from there.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That sounds good. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome. Take care.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Bye.
